title: Linked List Cycle
statement: A singly linked list is given by its values and by `pos`, the 0-based index of the node that the tail points at. `pos` is -1 when there is no cycle. Return true when a cycle exists. Use Floyd's algorithm, not the index.
hints: A set of node identities detects a repeat visit and uses linear memory.
Floyd uses two pointers. The fast pointer moves two steps and the slow pointer moves one.
If there is a cycle they meet. If the fast pointer reaches the end, there is no cycle.

approaches.name: Hash set of nodes
approaches.explanation: A repeated object identity means a cycle.

approaches.name: Floyd tortoise and hare
approaches.explanation: The fast pointer gains one step per iteration inside the cycle.

editorial: Build the list and, when pos is nonnegative, point the tail at that node. Then ignore pos. Advance slow by one and fast by two. A meeting proves a cycle because the only way two different speeds reunite on a finite chain is a loop. A null next pointer proves the list is finite and acyclic.
